source.title: NAMSG: An Efficient Method For Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Yushu Chen; Hao Jing; Wenlai Zhao; Zhiqiang Liu; Li'an Qiao; Wei Xue; H. Fu; Guang-Wen Yang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and reports validation accuracy on image-classification benchmarks, testing optimizer-related generalization with its own method and settings.
record.gate_note: MNIST and WikiText-2 results concern convergence speed, not held-out performance, so they are not rows. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out image-classification comparisons between established adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD. These bear on V4, although the supplied text does not establish that tuning was restricted to learning rates and decay schedules.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that ARSG improves convergence speed and generalization over the tested popular adaptive methods. Their ImageNet statement that ARSG surpasses SGD applies to ARSG2 at learning rate 0.02; ARSG1 at 0.01 is described as close to SGD.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces RSG and ARSG and compares their validation performance with established optimizers. For RSG, ARSG and ARSGB, only step size is selected by grid search; compared algorithms receive exhaustive grid search.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and training mode: CIFAR-10 fast and fine modes are distinguished; ImageNet reports separate ADAM and ARSG step sizes. The paper says larger step sizes are beneficial to generalization in CIFAR-10 fine mode.
record.problems: Generalization comparisons are limited to the tested datasets and models. ImageNet experiments run only once and report no uncertainty; CIFAR-10 values are maximum validation accuracies with standard deviations. The paper does not report training-error values alongside these validation metrics in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported held-out optimizer results were identified. MNIST and WikiText-2 experiment results are described as convergence-speed comparisons and are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.

Held-out language performance; tuning restricted specifically to learning rates and decay schedules; controlled broad-versus-limited tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD. Numerical training-performance comparisons are unavailable in the supplied text.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text omits the supplementary experimental procedures and readable figure curves. It says established comparators received exhaustive grid search, without identifying all tuned parameters. Maximum validation accuracy measures held-out performance, not a numerically established train–test gap. Proposed-method performance rows are excluded as requested; they therefore do not supply verdicts. This study is not an original source for V4.

versions.untested_parts: No width sweep or interpolation-threshold experiment.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language-benchmark held-out results; no broad optimizer-tuning comparison beyond the stated experiment procedures.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet-20, fine mode: Adam, NADAM and AMSGRAD versus momentum SGD.
relationships.reason: R2–R4 report maximum validation accuracies of 90.79%, 90.80% and 90.45%, versus 91.51% for SGD in R1; the exact tuning dimensions are unspecified.
relationships.display_finding: Reported maximum validation accuracy favored momentum SGD over Adam, NADAM, and AMSGRAD, but tuning dimensions were unspecified and these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet-20, fine mode: RANGER versus momentum SGD.
relationships.reason: R5 shows a smaller penalty, 91.02% versus 91.51% in R1, with reported standard deviations of 0.22 and 0.21 percentage points and no significance test.
relationships.display_finding: Reported RANGER accuracy of 91.02% versus momentum SGD's 91.51% remains unverified, with no significance test.

relationships.condition: ImageNet, ResNet-50: Adam at learning rates 0.0001 and 0.0002 versus SGD; one run per configuration.
relationships.reason: R10–R11 report 72.49% and 73.86% maximum top-1 validation accuracy versus 75.59% in R9; the text also explicitly reports faster convergence for Adam.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly converged faster but achieved lower maximum validation accuracy than SGD in single runs, and these comparisons remain unverified.
